title: autotune: default batching/caching profiles + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Customers with bursty traffic and mixed latency/cost targets were manually tuning batching and caching settings, and ops were frequently running ad-hoc quantization experiments. Motivation: Provide safe, production-ready defaults and an autotune feedback loop that recommends batching/caching/quant profiles per workload and expose unit-econ tooling for teams to understand $/token and latency tradeoffs. This PR introduces: 1) A new autotune engine (runtime/autotune) that observes request size/seqlen distributions and suggests batching/windowing defaults; 2) Default batching and KV-cache heuristics that can be enabled per-route via the API and console; 3) Quantization profile metadata and a lightweight scoring function so the autotuner can recommend quant variants by workload; 4) A CLI "uecon" tool that computes unit economics for a route given simulated traffic and cost profiles; 5) Instrumentation and dashboards (console + observability) to track recommended vs. applied profiles and expected cost delta. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + Linear links (ENG-2411) - [x] Runtime autotune core + unit tests - [x] Expose defaults in route config and console UI - [x] Add quant profile metadata and scoring - [x] Add uecon CLI + integration tests - [x] Docs: cost-optimization.md + console how-to - [x] Safety: conservative defaults, opt-in for automated rollout Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature flag `autotune.v2`. Initially the UI shows recommendations as suggestions; ops can approve or enable automatic rollout. Backwards compatibility: all defaults are opt-in; existing routes keep current settings unless user opts in. Testing and metrics: Unit tests cover the heuristics and scoring. Integration tests run the autotune pipeline with synthetic traces; we added a canary that ran on internal staging (staging cluster 3) for 48h. Observed impact on internal workload: estimated 18-27% token-cost reduction for long-sequence, low-per-request latency tolerance workloads; negligible latency regressions (+1-5ms p50). CI notes: first CI run had lint errors in console component and a flaky e2e that we fixed by increasing test timeouts. Why this is safe: recommendations are non-destructive, and automated rollouts use canary steps. Related: ENG-2460 (quant profile taxonomy), SUP-894 (customer request for unit economics).

release_notes: Introduce an opt-in autotune engine that recommends batching, KV-cache, and quantization profiles per route. Adds a uecon CLI to compute route-level unit economics and console suggestions UI. Safe defaults are opt-in and automated rollouts are canaryed. Estimated token-cost reduction 18-27% on specific workloads; see docs/cost-optimization.md for guidance.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated by feature flag `autotune.v2`. To enable automatic rollouts, set `route.config.autotune.auto_rollout=true` and ensure route labels do not include 'sla:low-latency'. Use cli/uecon to simulate cost impact before enabling. Dashboards available at observability -> autotune-recommendations.
risk_assessment: Low/Medium. Heuristics are conservative and have minimum sample windows. Automated rollout requires explicit opt-in. Integration tests and 48h staging canary performed. Monitor token-cost delta and latency p50/p95 during rollout.
